# WO-518: Runner: a run-time budget that never starves low-priority sites

## Goal
A scheduled run walks every enabled broker in priority order (`Runner.brokers`, `engine/runner.py:382-385`) and skips the ones not yet due (`runner.py:453-460`). With 400+ sites one run can take hours and the Windows task is killed after two hours (`scheduler/render.py:90`). Add an optional run-time budget (`max_run_s`, default None = unlimited, set by the scheduled path to 90 minutes in a later in-house change): when it is spent, no new broker is started and the report says how many were left. To avoid starving the low-priority sites, order the DUE brokers (those whose `next_check_at` is empty or in the past) by how overdue they are first, keeping priority only as the tie-break within the same day; brokers not due still go through the cheap "skipped_not_due" path first. The order change applies only when a budget is set, so every existing run is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. With a budget and 6 due brokers of different priority where the fake `process` takes 40 s each (fake clock) and `max_run_s=100`, exactly 3 brokers run; the remaining 3 are counted in a new `RunReport.deferred` integer (default 0).
2. On the next run (same fake store), the 3 deferred brokers run first (they are the most overdue), so after two runs all six have been processed once.
3. Without a budget the order is exactly `-priority, id` as today (golden list over a 20-broker fake registry).
4. A never-checked broker (no `next_check_at`) counts as the most overdue.
5. `RunReport.summary_lines` (`runner.py:104-130`) mentions deferred sites in plain words only when `deferred > 0`; with 0 it is unchanged.
6. Elapsed time uses an injectable monotonic clock; no sleeping in tests; cancellation and WO-513 timeouts still work.
7. Existing runner tests and WO-513/514 tests pass unchanged.
